ns2:section.sectionText: Topic Section R: Rhetoric and Race in Writing Studies The work of scholars of color has been substantial in shaping the field of rhetoric/composition/writing studies from its very beginnings. In this course we will read this work, following its arc from its considerable influence on linguistics, language policy, and literacy studies to its more recent contributions to the study of the practice and history of rhetoric. Texts will include: Geneva Smitherman, Talkin? and Testifyin?; Scott Lyons, X-Marks: Native Signatures of Assent; LuMing Mao, Reading Chinese Fortune Cookie; Victor Villaneuva, Bootstraps: From an American Academic of Color; Shirley Wilson Logan, Liberating Language: Sites of Rhetorical Education in Nineteenth Century Black America.
